title: SPE Chapter 04 — Views
_comment: VET THIS FILE before rendering. lane 'app' = running page (optional 'js' Base API); lane 'code' = self-contained page from local source, lines hl highlighted. Rebuild: RESYNTH=1 bash scripts/make-episode.sh 04-Views

scenes.narr: Chapter four looks identical once more, but inside, every plugin has split cleanly into two halves: a model and a view.
The model's job shrank to one thing — return data. Each action now hands back a plain array, a title and a body, with no HTML at all.
The view's job is the other half: turn that data array into HTML. A base view supplies a generic card, so simple pages need no view of their own.
Init now assembles both halves — it asks the model for data, finds the matching view, and merges the rendered HTML into the output.
This single line is the fallback: if a plugin has no view of its own, it quietly uses the base view — so a view is always optional.
The About page proves it: it has a model but no view, so the base view renders it, and to the eye nothing has changed.
Here is the most important habit in the whole series: one escaping helper, run over every value before it ever reaches the page.
Watch it work. The Home body deliberately contains bold tags written as text, and because output is escaped, they show as characters, not markup.
There they are on the page: the angle brackets shown literally, never interpreted. That is a whole class of injection attacks closed off by default.
Theme is now the only class that knows a complete HTML document — the shell, the head, the two sidebars — lifted entirely out of Init.
Even a value placed inside an attribute, like the contact email in this mailto link, passes through the very same escape.
Escaping at the boundary, every single time, is the one habit that keeps every later chapter safe.
And because the model returns pure data, that same page is still available as JSON, untouched by any of the view work.
That is chapter four: model for data, view for HTML, theme for the document, and escaping at the edge. Next, chapter five gives every class its own file.
